title: Inserting an element into an array
summary: Insert element 3 at index 1: first copy existing elements one position to the right starting from the end, then write the new element.
context: Array nums has 5 slots at indices 0 through 4. Its initial storage is [1, 2, 5, 4, 0], where only the first 4 elements [1, 2, 5, 4] are valid and the trailing 0 at index 4 is an unused placeholder. The goal is to insert 3 at index 1 while preserving the relative order of the existing valid elements.
result: After insertion, all 5 slots hold valid elements; the caller updates the valid length to 5 accordingly, whereas the sample insert function itself only assigns slot values. When the text later notes that the last element of a fixed-length array is "lost", in this example only the placeholder 0 in the last slot is overwritten, so none of the four original valid elements are lost. Had all 5 slots originally held valid elements, overwriting would lose the final valid element, requiring array expansion beforehand or rejecting the insertion.

frames.title: Inserting an element into an array
frames.explanation: Copying backward from the end toward the insertion point ensures that every element about to be overwritten and still needed has already been copied to the adjacent slot on its right. Copying does not clear the source slot, so duplicate values appear in intermediate states. Inserting into the middle of an array shifts O(n) elements on average.

prose.title: Inserting an element into an array
prose.summary: Insert element 3 at index 1: first copy existing elements one position to the right starting from the end, then write the new element.
context: Array nums has 5 slots at indices 0 through 4. The goal is to insert 3 at index 1 while preserving the relative order of the existing valid elements.

When the text later notes that the last element of a fixed-length array is "lost", in this example only the placeholder 0 in the last slot is overwritten, so none of the four original valid elements are lost. steps.title: Prepare for insertion
steps.explanation: Current storage is [1, 2, 5, 4, 0] with valid length 4, and the trailing 0 is a placeholder. Index 1 holds the valid element 2, so writing 3 directly would overwrite and lose it; the elements at indices 1 through 3 must first be copied to the right.
steps.key_state: Ready to insert 3 at index 1; current storage is [1, 2, 5, 4, 0], the valid sequence is [1, 2, 5, 4], and the trailing 0 is a placeholder.
steps.announcement: Show initial array [1, 2, 5, 4, 0] and prepare to shift existing elements right before inserting 3 at index 1.

steps.title: Copy the trailing 4
steps.explanation: Execute nums[4] = nums[3] to copy 4 to index 4, overwriting the placeholder 0. Current storage is [1, 2, 5, 4, 4]; since the 4 from index 3 is now preserved, index 3 can safely be overwritten in the next step. Because 3 has not been written yet, the valid length remains 4.
steps.key_state: Executed nums[4] = nums[3] to copy 4; current storage is [1, 2, 5, 4, 4].
steps.announcement: Execute nums[4] = nums[3] to copy 4 from index 3 to index 4, overwriting the placeholder 0.

steps.title: Copy 5
steps.explanation: Execute nums[3] = nums[2] to copy 5 to index 3, making current storage [1, 2, 5, 5, 4]. The original 4 is already saved in the last slot and will not be lost; next, 2 must still be copied before writing 3. The valid length remains 4.
steps.key_state: Executed nums[3] = nums[2] to copy 5; current storage is [1, 2, 5, 5, 4], with only 4 and 5 copied so far and 3 not yet written.
steps.announcement: Execute nums[3] = nums[2] to copy 5 from index 2 to index 3.

steps.title: Copy 2
steps.explanation: Execute nums[2] = nums[1] to copy 2 to index 2, making current storage [1, 2, 2, 5, 4]. The original elements 2, 5, and 4 have now shifted right; index 1 still holds 2, which can now be safely overwritten. Because 3 has not been written yet, the valid length remains 4.
steps.key_state: Executed nums[2] = nums[1] to copy 2; rightward shifting is complete, current storage is [1, 2, 2, 5, 4], and 3 is ready to be written.
steps.announcement: Execute nums[2] = nums[1] to copy 2 from index 1 to index 2; index 1 can now be safely overwritten.

steps.title: Write 3
steps.explanation: Execute nums[1] = 3, making current storage [1, 3, 2, 5, 4]. The new element is written and insertion is complete; the number of valid elements increases from 4 to 5, and the caller updates the valid length.
steps.key_state: Executed nums[1] = 3, giving final storage [1, 3, 2, 5, 4]; the caller updates the valid length to 5.
steps.announcement: Write 3 at index 1 to complete insertion, giving array [1, 3, 2, 5, 4]; the caller updates the valid length to 5.
